tasks.title: Decide whether to change what _generate_doc_id hashes - and how to migrate the ids already in the live DB
tasks.blocked_on: A human must decide whether to change the content-hash, because there is no migration path for doc_ids already stored in the live DB. THE DEFECT, measured and not disputed: _extract_pdf_text joins page text with a literal '--- PAGE BREAK ---' marker BEFORE _generate_doc_id hashes the first 10,000 words, so the same content ingested as .txt and as .pdf can never dedupe - on a real 19-page document the PDF's text WITHOUT the join hashes to cea9b4004347, an exact match to the live .txt document's id, and WITH it to f1aa9fc2b7da. The 72 injected marker words are the entire miss. THE OPTIONS: (a) leave it, and accept that a cross-format re-ingest silently creates a second unlinked document; (b) strip markers before hashing, which changes the id computed for every future re-ingest of an already-indexed PDF and needs a migration for the stored ids; (c) hash a normalised form and keep a compatibility id. TO-DOS.md already records this as 'a decision for a human to make deliberately (and to plan a migration for), not something to patch quietly inside a documentation task'
tasks.verify: Not runnable until the decision is taken. Once taken: the chosen behaviour is implemented, `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest test_card_updates.py test_sid_ingest.py test_repoint_document.py -q` passes, and if the hash changed, a migration is demonstrated against a COPY of the live DB - never the live one - showing what happens to existing doc_ids
tasks.why_model: a shared hashing function with a live database behind it; a plausible-but-wrong migration is expensive and hard to reverse
tasks.why_effort: the failure mode is a confident wrong answer that silently forks documents in a real corpus, and it must be understood before it is touched
tasks.why_mode: REQUIRES-USER: no amount of work resolves whether the stored ids may change; that is the human's call
tasks.why_lane: SERIAL: writes kb/core.py and kb/ingest/*, read or written by every other code task
